newsitem.title: MEXICO: Cemex creates fund for Asia expansions.
newsitem.headline: Cemex creates fund for Asia expansions.

text.p: Mexico-based cement giant Cemex SA took a further step toward its expansion into Southeast Asia by announcing the creation of a $300 million fund to finance the strategy.
The company announced the fund's creation during a conference with analysts earlier this week, from which Reuters obtained a recorded copy.

"Cemex is in the process of establishing a venture capital fund for its expansion in Southeast Asia. This fund will allow the company to participate in this high-growth region without a large capital commitment," Financial Director Rodrigo Trevino said.

"We expect the total size of the fund to be in the range of $300 million and anticipate Cemex's contribution will be in the range of $100 million," he added. Cemex looks to attract about 10 institutional investors to contribute to the fund, he added.
Trevino explained in the conference that Cemex hopes to attract investors with a long-term vision that knows the company's potential in the region.
Cemex would control the fund and apply its resources at its discretion in projects from new plants to purchasing complexes in ventures with local companies, he added.
Analysts applauded the new fund as a cautious move to help the company reduce its financial risk in the region.
"I believe it is a very prudent and intelligent measure," New York CS First Boston analyst Rafael Elias Linero said.

Cemex grew from a regional cement compnay to one of the world's top international cement players in a few years with expansions to Spain, Venezuela, the United States, the Caribbean and most recently in Colombia. The company's latest target area is Southeast Asia.
"Cemex continues to signal to the market its willingness to participate in the Asian region, and to proceed with a prudent investment model," Robert Flemings Research analyst Ben Uglow said.
Uglow added that the region is compelling in the long-term, having grown at high, more sustained rates than Latin America.
Caspian Securities' Paul Rodriguez called the fund "innovative," saying it lowers the company's risk and allows it to expand with a small capital investment.

Another aspect of the model proposed by Cemex is that even though the company would invest a little amount of money, and perhaps its participation in the projects will be a minority stake, the company would maintain managerial control and charge lucrative management fees, Rodriguez said.
Cemex did not specify the type of return it expected from capital invested in the fund, but Cemex's Trevino said it would be "significantly greater" than current levels.
